# Command line reference

<!-- Generated by go generate ./cmd/dummyrun from the commands' own help text. Do not edit. CI fails when this file is out of date. -->

Each section below is a command's own help text, copied from the program. To learn how the commands fit together, start with [ENGINE.md](ENGINE.md).

## dummyrun

The list of commands and the model providers.

```text
Usage:
  dummyrun run --cast DIR --persona ID --scenario ID|--scenario-file FILE --target CONFIG --out DIR \
      --browser chrome|firefox --provider PROVIDER --model MODEL [--region REGION] [--endpoint URL] \
      [--api-key-env NAME] [--project ID] [--reasoning-effort LEVEL] [--openai-api chat|responses] \
      [--batch ID] [--seed N] [--repeat-index N] [--universe sitemap|URL] [--session FILE] [--identify] [--respect-robots]
  dummyrun coverage --runs DIR [--build SHA] [--strata device|persona] [--confirmed-only=false] [--threshold NAME=VALUE]... \
      [--clusters FILE]... [--format json|markdown] [--out FILE] [--fail-unless-stopped]
  dummyrun report --runs DIR [--a11y FILE]... [--title TEXT] [--client TEXT] [--format html|md|json|sarif|junit] [--include pending] \
      [--baseline FILE] [--build SHA] [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--out FILE]
  dummyrun review RUNS_DIR|RECORD... [--list [--json] [--verdict V]] [--confirm ID]... [--reject ID]... [--reason TEXT] [--reviewer NAME]
  dummyrun a11y [--sitemap URL] [URL...] [--browser chrome|firefox] [--allow FILE] [--json FILE] [--session FILE] [--identify] [--respect-robots]
  dummyrun session save --target CONFIG --role ROLE --out FILE [--browser chrome|firefox]
  dummyrun doctor [--stop]
  dummyrun mcp [--allow-origin ORIGIN]... [--provider PROVIDER --model MODEL] [--cast DIR]... [--out DIR]
  dummyrun version

Run "dummyrun run -h", "dummyrun coverage -h", "dummyrun report -h", "dummyrun review -h", "dummyrun a11y -h", "dummyrun session -h", "dummyrun mcp -h" or "dummyrun doctor -h" for every flag. "dummyrun audit a11y" is the same as "dummyrun a11y".

Providers:
  azure              Azure OpenAI. --endpoint or DUMMYRUN_AZURE_ENDPOINT; sign in with "az login" or another
                     DefaultAzureCredential source. --region is required.
  openai-compatible  Any OpenAI-style service or local server. --endpoint is the base URL, such as
                     https://api.openai.com/v1 or http://localhost:11434/v1. --api-key-env names the variable
                     that holds the key (leave it out for a local server). --region is required (use "local").
  anthropic          Anthropic Messages API. The key is read from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or --api-key-env.
  gemini             Gemini Developer API. The key is read from GEMINI_API_KEY or --api-key-env.
  vertex             Gemini on Vertex AI with Application Default Credentials. --project (or
                     GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT) and --region are required.
  bedrock            Amazon Bedrock Converse with the AWS default credential chain. --region defaults to eu-west-2.

An API key is read from the environment when the run starts. It is never printed or written to a run record.
The same holds for the test-user credentials named in a target file's signin block.
```

## dummyrun run

Play one persona through one scenario and write a run record.

```text
Usage of run:
  -api-key-env string
    	name of the environment variable that holds the API key
  -api-version string
    	Azure OpenAI API version (default 2025-04-01-preview)
  -batch string
    	batch ID grouping runs started together
  -browser string
    	chrome or firefox (default "chrome")
  -cast string
    	cast directory
  -endpoint string
    	base URL of the provider (Azure endpoint, or the OpenAI-compatible base URL)
  -headful
    	show the browser window
  -identify
    	add "DummyRun/<version> (+https://dummyrun.dev/scanner/)" to the browser's user agent (also set by "identify": true in the target file)
  -model string
    	deployment or model name
  -openai-api string
    	OpenAI-style API: chat (default) or responses, for models that need it to call tools
  -out string
    	directory for run records
  -persona string
    	persona ID
  -project string
    	Google Cloud project for the vertex provider
  -provider string
    	model provider: azure, openai-compatible, anthropic, gemini, vertex, bedrock (default "azure")
  -reasoning-effort string
    	reasoning effort for OpenAI-style models: none, minimal, low, medium, high or xhigh
  -region string
    	region the model runs in, such as uksouth or global (optional where the provider has a default)
  -repeat-index int
    	which repeat this is for the persona, scenario and model in the batch; -1 counts the records already in --out (default -1)
  -respect-robots
    	fetch robots.txt from the target origin and block what it disallows for DummyRun or * (also set by "respect_robots": true in the target file); a site-wide disallow stops the run before the browser starts
  -scenario string
    	scenario ID
  -seed int
    	sampling seed (0 or more), sent to providers that take one; the record shows null where it was not sent (default -1)
  -session string
    	sign in from this saved session file (see "dummyrun session save") instead of the login form
  -steps int
    	step budget override (up to 40)
  -target string
    	target configuration (JSON)
  -tokens int
    	token budget (input plus output)
  -universe string
    	where the routes that exist come from, for route coverage: "sitemap" (base_url/sitemap.xml) or a sitemap URL
```

## dummyrun coverage

Count what a set of run records covers, with the limits of each number. See [COVERAGE.md](COVERAGE.md).

```text
Usage of coverage:
  -build string
    	commit or build hash to count (at least 7 characters); needed when the records come from more than one build
  -clusters value
    	a reviewer's grouping of findings into problems, JSON {"clusters": [["run/finding", ...]]}; give two files for kappa
  -confirmed-only
    	count only reviewer-confirmed findings; --confirmed-only=false also counts pending ones and labels the report a demonstration (default true)
  -fail-unless-stopped
    	exit 3 when the stopping rule is not satisfied, so a CI job can use it
  -format string
    	json or markdown (default "markdown")
  -out string
    	write the report to this file instead of standard output
  -runs value
    	directory or file of run records; repeat the flag to read several
  -strata string
    	what the stopping rule treats as separate groups: device or persona (default "device")
  -threshold value
    	policy number as name=value, repeatable: coverage (default 0.90), min-runs (4), no-new (3), kappa (0.6)
```

## dummyrun report

Turn run records and accessibility sweep results into an audit report. See [REPORT.md](REPORT.md) and [BADGES.md](BADGES.md).

```text
Usage: dummyrun report --runs DIR|FILE [--runs ...] [--a11y FILE]... [--title TEXT] [--client TEXT]
    [--format html|md|json|sarif|junit|badge|shields] [--include pending] [--baseline FILE] [--build SHA] [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--out FILE]

Turns run records and accessibility sweep results into an audit report. The default is one self-contained
HTML file. It shows only the findings a reviewer has confirmed. Add --include pending to show the rest,
marked not reviewed. Rejected findings never appear. The report covers a sample of pages and makes no
claim of WCAG conformance.
--format badge writes a small SVG badge and --format shields writes the shields.io endpoint JSON for it.
Both say how many findings are open and the date of the newest run.
  -a11y value
    	JSON file from dummyrun a11y --json; repeatable
  -baseline string
    	an earlier report in JSON form; each finding is marked new or still present, and fixed ones are listed
  -build string
    	commit or build hash to report on (at least 7 characters); default is every record given
  -client string
    	free text naming who the report is for
  -date string
    	report date as YYYY-MM-DD (default today)
  -format string
    	html, md, json, sarif, junit, badge (SVG) or shields (shields.io endpoint JSON) (default "html")
  -include string
    	"pending" also includes findings no reviewer has confirmed, marked not reviewed (default: confirmed only)
  -out string
    	write the report to this file instead of standard output
  -runs value
    	directory or file of run records; repeat the flag to read several (record paths may also follow the flags)
  -title string
    	report title (default "Accessibility and usability audit")
```

## dummyrun review

Confirm or reject the pending findings in run records. Only confirmed findings reach a report. See [ENGINE.md](ENGINE.md).

```text
Usage of review:
  -confirm value
    	confirm the pending findings with this fingerprint, a fingerprint prefix (6 or more characters), run/finding or a finding ID; repeatable
  -json
    	with --list, print JSON instead of a table
  -list
    	list the problems and change nothing
  -reason value
    	why, given once for the whole command: required with --reject, optional with --confirm
  -reject value
    	reject the pending findings with this fingerprint, prefix, run/finding or finding ID; needs --reason; repeatable
  -reviewer string
    	who is reviewing (default: git config user.name)
  -verdict string
    	with --list, which findings to show: pending, confirmed, rejected or all (default "pending")
```

## dummyrun a11y

Check pages for WCAG 2.2 A and AA failures with no model. `dummyrun audit a11y` is the same command.

```text
Usage:
  dummyrun a11y [--sitemap URL] [--rebase URL] [URL...] [flags]

Runs the axe-core WCAG 2.2 A and AA rules on each page in a real browser. No model is called.

Flags:
  --sitemap URL     a sitemap (or sitemap index) listing the pages to test
  --rebase URL      move every sitemap URL onto this origin, to test a local copy of a site
  --browser NAME    chrome or firefox (default chrome)
  --viewport NAME   desktop (1280), phone (375), small (320) or both (desktop and phone, the default)
  --scheme NAME     light, dark or both (default both)
  --text-scale N    the system text size in percent, 100 to 300, such as 200. A comma-separated list such as
                    100,200 tests each size. The browser's default font size is raised and the page is not zoomed,
                    so rem and em text grows and px text may not. A size above 100 turns on --layout
  --layout          also run the layout checks: sideways overflow, cut-off text in controls, overlapping controls
                    and targets under 24 by 24 CSS px. Rules dummyrun-reflow, dummyrun-clipped-text,
                    dummyrun-overlap and dummyrun-target-size. They fail the sweep like axe rules and the
                    allow-list can accept them
  --screenshots DIR write a PNG crop of the elements the layout checks flag into DIR, at most 12 for each page and
                    setting
  --allow FILE      accepted violations, one per line: rule | page | selector | reason
  --json FILE       write the full report as JSON; "-" writes it to standard output
  --identify        add "DummyRun/<version> (+https://dummyrun.dev/scanner/)" to the browser's user agent
  --respect-robots  fetch robots.txt from each page's origin and skip pages it disallows for DummyRun or *
  --session FILE    a saved session (see "dummyrun session save"), loaded before the first page so the pages are
                    tested signed in. The file holds cookies: keep it private
  --headful         show the browser window

Exit status: 0 when nothing fails, 1 when a violation is not in the allow-list or a page cannot be
tested, 2 for a usage error, 3 when robots.txt disallows every page. Pages skipped for robots.txt do not fail the sweep.
```

## dummyrun doctor

List browsers and profile directories that an earlier run left behind, and stop them with `--stop`.

```text
Usage of doctor:
  -stop
    	stop the browsers listed and remove their profile directories
```

## dummyrun session

Sign in once through a target's login form and save the session for reuse. See [ENGINE.md](ENGINE.md).

```text
Usage:
  dummyrun session save --target CONFIG --role ROLE --out FILE [--browser chrome|firefox] [--headful]

Signs in once through the login form named in the target file, with the credentials in the role's
environment variables, and writes the browser's cookies and local storage to FILE. The file is in
Playwright's storageState format. "dummyrun run --session FILE" and "dummyrun a11y --session FILE" load it
instead of signing in, so CI can reuse one sign-in.

The file holds live session cookies. It is written with mode 0600. Keep it out of version control and
treat it like a password. The command prints how many cookies it saved, the role and the file path, and never a cookie's value.

Flags:
  --target CONFIG   the target file; it needs a signin block
  --role ROLE       which of the target's credentials roles to sign in as
  --out FILE        where to write the session
  --browser NAME    chrome or firefox (default chrome)
  --headful         show the browser window
```

## dummyrun mcp

Serve Dummy Run to a coding agent over the Model Context Protocol. See [MCP.md](MCP.md).

```text
Usage:
  dummyrun mcp [--allow-origin ORIGIN]... [--cast DIR]... [--out DIR] [--browser chrome|firefox] [flags]

Serves four tools to a coding agent over standard input and output, using the Model Context Protocol:
list_personas, a11y_sweep, run_persona and get_run. Standard output carries only the protocol.

Sites:
  --allow-origin ORIGIN   a site the tools may test, besides localhost, 127.0.0.1 and private-network hosts.
                          A host, a wildcard such as *.example.com or an origin such as https://preview.example.com.
                          Repeat the flag, or set DUMMYRUN_MCP_ALLOW_ORIGINS to a comma-separated list.

Files:
  --cast DIR              a folder of local personas. Repeat for more. The default is each folder in ./casts
                          except library. The built-in library is always available.
  --out DIR               where run records go, and the only place get_run reads (default
                          ~/.local/share/dummyrun/runs/mcp)

Limits:
  --max-steps N           step cap for one run_persona call (default 25; a call asks for 10 unless it says more)
  --max-tokens N          token cap for one run_persona call (default 400000)
  --session-tokens N      total model tokens for the session (default 1000000)
  --max-runs N            run_persona calls per session (default 10)
  --max-sweeps N          a11y_sweep calls per session (default 40)

Model provider, for run_persona only. Each flag also reads the variable shown:
  --provider NAME         DUMMYRUN_PROVIDER (default azure)
  --model NAME            DUMMYRUN_MODEL
  --region NAME           DUMMYRUN_REGION
  --endpoint URL          DUMMYRUN_ENDPOINT, and DUMMYRUN_AZURE_ENDPOINT for azure
  --api-key-env NAME      DUMMYRUN_API_KEY_ENV
  --project ID            DUMMYRUN_PROJECT
  --reasoning-effort L    DUMMYRUN_REASONING_EFFORT
  --openai-api KIND       DUMMYRUN_OPENAI_API
  --api-version V         DUMMYRUN_API_VERSION

Other:
  --browser NAME          chrome or firefox (default chrome)
  --verbose               write the engine's progress lines to standard error
```

## dummyrun-otel

Send run records to an OpenTelemetry backend and Grafana.

```text
Usage:
  dummyrun-otel export [flags] FILE|DIR...   send run records to an OTLP endpoint
  dummyrun-otel watch  [flags] DIR           send new run records as they appear
  dummyrun-otel version

The OTLP endpoint, headers and TLS settings come from the standard variables:
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL,
OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES. Grafana annotations need --grafana-url and GRAFANA_TOKEN.
Run "dummyrun-otel export -h" for the flags.
```

## dummyrun-otel export

Send the records in the files or directories you name, once.

```text
Usage of dummyrun-otel export:
  -dry-run
    	print what would be sent as JSON and send nothing
  -grafana-url string
    	Grafana base URL for annotations; the token comes from GRAFANA_TOKEN
  -logs-max-age duration
    	skip log records older than this, because Loki rejects them by default; 0 sends every record (default 168h0m0s)
  -metrics-temporality string
    	metric temporality: cumulative or delta (default "cumulative")
  -protocol string
    	OTLP transport: http/protobuf (default) or grpc
  -signals string
    	what to send, a comma separated list of traces, metrics, logs and annotations; use it to send only what an earlier export missed. Annotations also need --grafana-url (default "traces,metrics,logs,annotations")
  -timeout duration
    	how long to wait for the final flush (default 30s)
  -verify-loki string
    	Loki base URL; after the export, count the log lines back per run and fail when any are missing. Basic auth comes from LOKI_BASIC_AUTH as user:password
```

## dummyrun-otel watch

Send each new record in a directory as it appears.

```text
Usage of dummyrun-otel watch:
  -dry-run
    	print what would be sent as JSON and send nothing
  -existing
    	also send the records already in the directory at start
  -grafana-url string
    	Grafana base URL for annotations; the token comes from GRAFANA_TOKEN
  -interval duration
    	how often to look for new files (default 5s)
  -logs-max-age duration
    	skip log records older than this, because Loki rejects them by default; 0 sends every record (default 168h0m0s)
  -metrics-temporality string
    	metric temporality: cumulative or delta (default "cumulative")
  -protocol string
    	OTLP transport: http/protobuf (default) or grpc
  -signals string
    	what to send, a comma separated list of traces, metrics, logs and annotations; use it to send only what an earlier export missed. Annotations also need --grafana-url (default "traces,metrics,logs,annotations")
  -timeout duration
    	how long to wait for the final flush (default 30s)
  -verify-loki string
    	Loki base URL; after the export, count the log lines back per run and fail when any are missing. Basic auth comes from LOKI_BASIC_AUTH as user:password
```
